name: Abstracted speed
summary: A stand-in for the many loci that set a horse's speed. One allele raises it, one lowers it, and the two copies add. The real trait is polygenic; this single locus is an abstraction, not a claim about a real gene.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Ordinary speed for whatever the horse's own speed genes say - which, since most horses carry a copy of this one, is itself slightly unusual.

phenotypes.name: Slower
phenotypes.description: One sluggish copy. The same thing in reverse: slower by the percentage on that copy, usually around a tenth, and inherited with the allele.

phenotypes.name: Much slower
phenotypes.description: Two sluggish copies, and the percentages subtract together. Around a fifth under on average and a great deal less at the extreme.

phenotypes.name: Faster
phenotypes.description: One swift copy. The horse is faster than its own genes would make it, by the percentage written on that copy - usually around a tenth. It passes that exact percentage on with the allele.

phenotypes.name: Balanced
phenotypes.description: One swift copy and one sluggish copy. Their percentages very nearly cancel, so the horse runs close to its ordinary speed while carrying, and passing on, both extremes.

phenotypes.name: Much faster
phenotypes.description: Two swift copies, and the percentages add. Around a fifth over on average, and far more when both copies rolled well - the fastest horses in the world are bred here, because no wild horse is born with two.
